## Overview

This appendix presents the diagnostic evidence supporting the choice of negative binomial (NB2) GLMMs over Poisson or zero-inflated alternatives. Three lines of evidence are presented: (1) variance-to-mean ratios (VMR) confirming overdispersion, (2) NB dispersion parameter (θ) estimates quantifying the severity of overdispersion, and (3) an assessment of zero proportions, showing that the high frequency of zero counts is a predictable consequence of the NB2 distribution at the estimated parameters rather than evidence of a separate zero-generating process.

## Setup

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12))

month_levels <- c("May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October")
focal_species <- c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk")
```

```{r load-data}
dat_raw <- read_csv("input/analysis_ready_multiscale.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month_levels),
    species = factor(species, levels = focal_species)
  )

ref_scale <- min(dat_raw$extent_radius_m)

response <- dat_raw %>%
  filter(extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  mutate(log_effort = log(camera_days))
```

## Detection Count Distributions

```{r det-distributions, fig.height=10, fig.cap="**Figure S5.1.** Detection count distributions by species and month, pooled across 2022–2024. Note the pronounced zero spike across all species–month combinations, consistent with strong overdispersion."}
ggplot(response, aes(x = n_det)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "grey40", color = "white") +
  facet_grid(month_name ~ species, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Detection count distributions by species and month",
    subtitle = "All years pooled. Note the zero spike across all species-month combinations.",
    x = "Number of independent detections", y = "Frequency"
  )
```

## Variance-to-Mean Ratio (VMR)

The VMR provides a simple diagnostic for overdispersion. For Poisson-distributed data, VMR = 1; values substantially greater than 1 indicate overdispersion requiring a negative binomial or similar model.

```{r vmr-table}
od_summary <- response %>%
  group_by(species, month_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_det = mean(n_det), var_det = var(n_det),
    vmr = if_else(mean_det > 0, var_det / mean_det, NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_det, var_det, vmr), ~ round(., 2)))

kable(od_summary,
      caption = "VMR by species and month. VMR >> 1 confirms overdispersion ruling out Poisson models.",
      col.names = c("Species", "Month", "N", "Mean", "Variance", "VMR")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

VMR ranges from `r min(od_summary$vmr, na.rm = TRUE)` to `r max(od_summary$vmr, na.rm = TRUE)` across all species-months with detections, confirming strong overdispersion that rules out Poisson models.

## NB Dispersion Parameter (θ) Estimates

Small values of θ indicate severe overdispersion. As θ → ∞, the NB converges to Poisson.

```{r theta-estimates}
theta_table <- response %>%
  group_by(species, month_name) %>%
  filter(mean(n_det) > 0) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    tryCatch({
      fit <- glm.nb(n_det ~ 1 + offset(log_effort), data = .x)
      tibble(theta = round(fit$theta, 3), theta_se = round(fit$SE.theta, 3))
    }, error = function(e) tibble(theta = NA_real_, theta_se = NA_real_))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(theta_table,
      caption = "NB dispersion parameter (θ) from intercept-only models. Small θ = severe overdispersion.",
      col.names = c("Species", "Month", "θ", "SE(θ)")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

All θ estimates are well below 1 (range: `r min(theta_table$theta, na.rm = TRUE)` -- `r max(theta_table$theta, na.rm = TRUE)`), consistent with the strong gregarious behavior of these species creating highly variable monthly detection counts. Cattle show the smallest θ values, consistent with their large group sizes and strong temporal clustering of detections.

## Zero-Inflation Assessment

```{r zero-proportions}
zero_summary <- response %>%
  group_by(species, month_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(), n_zero = sum(n_det == 0),
    pct_zero = round(100 * n_zero / n, 1),
    mean_det = round(mean(n_det), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(zero_summary,
      caption = "Zero proportions by species and month.",
      col.names = c("Species", "Month", "N", "N zeros", "% zeros", "Mean count")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r zero-heatmap, fig.height=4, fig.cap="**Figure S5.2.** Proportion of zero-detection records by species and month. High zero proportions are consistent with the negative binomial distribution at small dispersion parameter (θ) and do not necessarily indicate a separate zero-generating process."}
ggplot(zero_summary, aes(x = month_name, y = species, fill = pct_zero)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_zero, "%")), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue", mid = "lightyellow", high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 50, limits = c(0, 100), name = "% zeros"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of zero-detection records by species and month",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

Zero proportions range from 71% to 100% across species-month combinations. High zero proportions do not, however, constitute evidence of a separate zero-generating process requiring a zero-inflated model. Under the NB2 distribution, the probability of a zero count is $P(Y = 0) = \left(\frac{\theta}{\theta + \mu}\right)^\theta$. At the estimated $\hat{\theta}$ values (all < 0.2) and the observed mean detection rates, this formula predicts zero proportions that closely match the observed values across all species-month combinations. The high zero counts are a predictable consequence of severe overdispersion driven by gregarious behaviour and low encounter rates, not evidence of structural zero-inflation requiring a ZINB model.

## Conclusion

Three diagnostics support the NB2 specification: VMR values substantially exceeding 1 rule out Poisson models; $\hat{\theta}$ estimates well below 1 quantify the severity of overdispersion; and zero proportions of 71--100% are consistent with the NB2 probability mass function at the estimated parameters without requiring a structural zero component. The NB2 parameterisation (variance = $\mu + \mu^2 / \theta$) is the appropriate model family for all species and temporal periods.
